pr_title: arch: arc: clear MPU regions before init it to fix tests exception and timeout
pr_body:
EMSK boards can't be reset between tests due to board hardware design. 
But MPU v3 assume that all the MPU registers has been reset to zero. 
During sanitycheck tests, MPU configs of previous test could pass to following tests and cause exceptions. 
This PR fixes this issue by adding MPU region reset. 
The issue was only found on MPU v3, so this fix does not apply to MPU v2.

Fixes #28493
pr_comments:
This looks OK to me.
I just feel that eventually we need to make a decision whether Zephyr should really initialize every ARCH-level hardware once it is coming out of reset or it should keep relying on the parent image, e.g. a bootloader... Right now we are not consistent across architectures and platforms.

> This looks OK to me.
> I just feel that eventually we need to make a decision whether Zephyr should really initialize every ARCH-level hardware once it is coming out of reset or it should keep relying on the parent image, e.g. a bootloader... Right now we are not consistent across architectures and platforms.

So are there any similar hacks done for other boards/arches? I'm asking because IMHO it would be logical to use some unified ifdef for them so that we may:
1. Document it and use similarly across the board
2. Easier remove all that mess if we decide to rely solely on clean out-of-reset state

> So are there any similar hacks done for other boards/arches? I'm asking because IMHO it would be logical to use some unified ifdef for them so that we may:

> Document it and use similarly across the board
> Easier remove all that mess if we decide to rely solely on clean out-of-reset state

Yes, at least Cortex-M is doing similar things, everywhere in the system init code. 

I guess the Kconfig switch should be something like `config ARCH_INIT_HW_AT_BOOT` and should be used explicitly around code that initializes ARCH core hardware to its default values, if it were coming out of warm reset.
@abrodkin if you would like to open a GH ticket for this, I can fill it in with the information about ARM.
